comment: Every real checkpoint the parity and triage suites load, with the source that serves it and the converter that puts it in the module's layout. `fetch.py` reads this. Sizes are the bytes the source reported when the entry was added; a mismatch means the source changed under us, which is worth knowing before a parity number moves. Most assets download from `url`; `gdrive` names a Google Drive file id and `extract` a member path inside a zip at `url`, for the two releases served no other way.

assets.note: Depth Anything 3 monocular (DA3-SMALL, Apache-2.0). Already a PyTorch-layout safetensors NFKMLXDepthAnything3.loadWeights reads directly: every branch loads, all 437 tensors: model.backbone.pretrained.* (the DinoV2 vits backbone with rope/qknorm/camera-token/cat_token from block 4), the model.head.* DualDPT depth AND aux/ray branches, model.cam_dec.*, and model.cam_enc.*. 4-D convs transpose to NHWC; the two resize_layers ConvT weights take the transposed-conv axis order [C_in,C_out,kH,kW]->[C_out,kH,kW,C_in], NOT a regular conv's. head.scratch.output_conv2_aux.0.2 is a SHARED nn.LayerNorm instance the state dict saves once, so the loader copies it onto levels 1-3. The reference (IK_VAL_DEPTH3_REF) is produced by `run_reference.py depth3 <out> --checkpoint <this> --size 518` under the da3 oracle env with IK_REF_SRC pointing at the unpacked `depth_anything_3` pip package; it records the 4 hooked features, the 4 head stages, the fused map, the pre-exp logits, the exp-depth output, the aux pyramid, the ray map and its confidence, the 4 camera tokens, the pose encoding, and the camera encoder's input and tokens.
the x3 release: ONE ×3 pixel-shuffle stage where x4 runs two ×2 stages, so it fits only the x3 geometry

Silero VAD v6 (snakers4). The released .jit carries a 16 kHz `_model.*` branch and an 8 kHz `_model_8k.*` branch; the converter keeps the 16 kHz branch. The parity record is produced by `run_reference.py silero_vad` under the llm oracle env, which needs the `silero-vad` package (its wrapper streams 512-sample chunks and threads the LSTM state); the converter needs only torch. `bytes` pins the master file, so a drift fails loudly.

The Descript Audio Codec, 44.1 kHz 8 kbps (9 codebooks). The released `.pth` wraps a weight-normalized `state_dict`; the converter extracts it in PyTorch layout and the loader fuses and transposes. The parity record is produced by `run_reference.py dac` under the llm oracle env, which needs the `descript-audio-codec` package (the encode/decode reference); the converter needs only torch.

SNAC 24 kHz multi-scale speech codec (3 codebooks at strides [4,2,1], depthwise convs, a decoder noise block, no bottleneck attention). The release's convolutions are weight-normalized through torch's parametrization API (`parametrizations.weight.original0/1`); the converter keeps them and the loader fuses. The parity record is produced by `run_reference.py snac` under the llm oracle env (needs `snac`), with the decoder noise block disabled so the reconstruction is deterministic.

SigLIP 2 base-patch16-224, the CLIP upgrade / VLM vision tower. The release is ALREADY a PyTorch-layout safetensors the loader reads directly (transposing the 4-D patch conv, mapping the vision_model./text_model. prefixes), so the converter is a passthrough normalizer. Most of the 1.5 GB is the 256k multilingual text embedding table. Parity via `run_reference.py siglip2` (llm oracle env, transformers >= 4.51). The architecture is SigLIP v1 (model_type 'siglip'); '2' is the training.

Tiny AutoEncoder for SD, the fast preview decoder. TWO release files (taesd_encoder.pth + taesd_decoder.pth, GitHub, ~5 MB each); the converter combines them into encoder.*/decoder.* keys and the [Module]-array loader matches the numeric Sequential keys directly. Parity via `run_reference.py taesd` (madebyollin's own taesd.py, vendored in sources/).

IP-Adapter for Stable Diffusion 1.5 (h94/IP-Adapter, ~44 MB, Apache-2.0). Holds image_proj.{proj,norm}.* (the CLIP-image-embedding projection) and ip_adapter.<N>.to_{k,v}_ip.weight (the per-cross-attention key/value). NFKMLXIPAdapter.load reads it directly and attaches the key/value to NFKMLXSDUNet's cross-attentions; the layer order is down->up->mid, because UNet2DConditionModel registers the mid block last, which is the order the adapter's numeric indices follow. Validated wired into the real SD 1.5 UNet against diffusers (run_reference.py ip_adapter_unet under the diffusers env, IK_VAL_IPADAPTER + IK_SD15_DIR -> IK_PARITY_IP_ADAPTER_UNET), cosine ~1e-12. The native .pth reader loads it directly; the keys are the reference's own `body.N` flat ModuleList, which the port holds as a [Module] array so the PReLU slots keep their indices. Record: `run_reference.py realesrgan_compact <out> --checkpoint <this>` under the llm oracle env (torch alone; the architecture is inlined in the mode) -> IK_PARITY_REALESRGAN_GENERAL_V3.

Zero-DCE++ (`enhance_net_nopool`), the authors' successor to Zero-DCE: depthwise-separable convolutions (`CSDN_Tem`), ONE shared three-channel curve reused across all eight iterations, and an estimator run at 1/12 resolution with the curve map lifted back by an align-corners bilinear upsample. Keys carry a `module.` prefix from the training wrapper, which the loader strips. Record: `run_reference.py zero_dce_plus <out> --checkpoint <this>` under the llm oracle env -> IK_PARITY_ZERO_DCE_PLUS.

IS-Net (`ISNetDIS`, the DIS project), U2-Net's successor by the same authors. The native .pth reader loads it directly and `NFKMLXU2Net.remapReferenceKey` translates the shared `rebnconvN` names, because the Residual U-blocks are U2-Net's unchanged. What differs: a stride-2 `conv_in` stem with no norm and no activation, wider stages, and six separate side maps with no fusion `outconv`. Record: `run_reference.py isnet <out> --checkpoint <this> --size 1024` under the llm oracle env with IK_REF_SRC pointing at a `dis/` directory holding the repository's `IS-Net/models/isnet.py`; it records the stem, stage 1, stage 6, and the five coarser side maps beside the prediction -> IK_PARITY_ISNET.

The normalized VGG-19 AdaIN encodes with (MIT). Its first 1x1 convolution carries the input normalization, so the plate reaches it unnormalized. The port keeps the truncated prefix through relu4_1 (index 30), which is the slice the reference takes. Loaded by NFKMLXAdaIN.loadEncoderWeights.

The AdaIN decoder that inverts relu4_1 features back to an image (MIT). Keys carry a `net.` prefix from the training wrapper, which both the loader and the oracle strip. Record: `run_reference.py adain <out> --checkpoint <this> --size 256` under the llm oracle env, with IK_ADAIN_VGG naming the encoder beside it and IK_REF_SRC pointing at an `adain/` directory holding naoto0804's `net.py` and `function.py`; it records both feature maps and the normalized features beside the decoded image -> IK_PARITY_ADAIN.

HAT-L x4 (the Hybrid Attention Transformer, XPixelGroup), SwinIR's successor: 12 groups of 6 blocks, 180 wide, 6 heads, window 16, overlap ratio 0.5, mlp ratio 2, compress ratio 3, squeeze factor 30. The tensors sit under `params_ema`, which the native reader unwraps. The two `relative_position_index_*` buffers are recomputed from the window geometry and dropped at load; the parity test compares both against these buffers, because the overlapping index relies on PyTorch reading NEGATIVE indices from the end of the bias table. Record: `run_reference.py hat <out> --checkpoint <this> --size 64` under the llm oracle env with IK_HAT_GROUPS=12 and IK_REF_SRC pointing at a `hat/` directory holding `hat_arch.py` (basicsr is shimmed in the mode) -> IK_PARITY_HAT_L.

Real-HAT-GAN x4 sharper: the HAT BASE geometry (6 groups, not 12) trained for real-world degradation, which is what measures the `.base` configuration. Record: `run_reference.py hat` with IK_HAT_GROUPS=6 -> IK_PARITY_REAL_HAT_GAN.

A SEEDED checkpoint from the reference `transformer_net.py` was tried and REJECTED: the network is trained to emit 0...255, so with random weights its output is near-zero noise (range about +-1.5 before the divide by 255) and the cosine measures the port's noise floor rather than the model — it scored 0.68, which looks like a failure and means nothing. Same trap as matting on a synthetic plate. The recorded 0.9999926 was measured on the official checkpoint; re-running it needs that file to reappear or a mirror to be found.

sources.comment: Reference implementations the oracles import. `IK_REF_SRC` points at <root>/refsrc; the three models whose reference is a whole small package get their own variable. Paths are relative to the source root. The sam2 entries reconstruct the package the SAM 2 oracles import: it cannot be pip-installed here (it needs Python >= 3.10) and was previously vendored by hand, which left that oracle unreproducible. An entry with an empty URL is an empty __init__.py.

releases_comment: A diffusion release is a directory of files rather than one checkpoint, so it is fetched whole and used in place — the port's `NFKMLXSDReleaseFiles(directoryURL:)` reads the released tree directly, and no conversion step applies. `text_encoder` and `vae` files a release publishes in half precision load through `NFKMLXWeightPrecision.float32`, which is the precision the parity records were measured at.

releases.note: The reference text-to-image pipeline for the `sd_text_encoder`, `sd_tokenizer`, and `sd_text_to_image` oracles.

stabilityai/stable-diffusion-2-1-base is GATED and returns 401 without a credential. This is an ungated release of the same lineage and geometry (cross-attention 1024, heads [5, 10, 20, 20], linear projection, OpenCLIP text tower), at the 768 v-prediction settings — which also exercises the sampler's velocity path. Its `model_index.json` names a safety checker whose `feature_extractor/` it does not ship, so those two entries are removed before the reference pipeline loads it. Its text encoder and autoencoder are published in bfloat16.
Published only in half precision; every parity run loads it at float32.

The smallest Qwen3 dense decoder, 1.4 GB. Its checkpoint ships lm_head.weight even though tie_word_embeddings is true; the two tensors are byte-identical, so the loader drops the duplicate rather than building a projection the tied model does not have.

The Qwen3-0.6B dense decoder fine-tuned as a text embedder, 1.2 GB. Its architecture is Qwen3ForCausalLM (model_type qwen3), so NFKMLXLanguage.configuration reads it unchanged; the embedder reads the base model's last hidden state, pools the LAST token (the tokenizer appends <|endoftext|>, whose position it reads), and L2-normalizes. Its embedding vocabulary is 151669, and its embeddings are tied.

EmbeddingGemma-300M, 1.2 GB. google/embeddinggemma-300m is gated; unsloth/embeddinggemma-300m is a faithful ungated mirror (the project uses mirrors for gated repos, as SD 2.1 does). The backbone is Gemma3TextModel (model_type gemma3_text) with use_bidirectional_attention true, NOT the causal Gemma 4 (gemma4_text) NFKMLXGemmaLanguage implements: `(1+w)` RMS norm (Gemma 3), sandwich norms, dual RoPE (local 10000 / global 1000000), sliding-window pattern 6 (window 512), QK-norm, GeGLU gelu_tanh, no value norm, no per-layer embeddings, no softcapping. The sentence-transformers head is mean pooling → Dense 768->3072 → Dense 3072->768 (both no-bias, Identity) → L2. Prompts: query 'task: search result | query: ', document 'title: none | text: '.

gte-reranker-modernbert-base, 0.6 GB. A ModernBertForSequenceClassification cross-encoder reranker: a bidirectional ModernBERT encoder over a [CLS] query [SEP] document [SEP] pair, mean-pooled, through a prediction head (dense + gelu + LayerNorm) and a single-logit classifier -> a relevance score. ModernBERT is RoPE (global theta 160000 every 3rd layer, local theta 10000 with a 128 sliding window elsewhere), GeGLU (Wi -> input,gate; act(input)*gate), LayerNorm throughout (norm_bias false), bias-free attention/mlp, no absolute position embeddings; layer 0's attn_norm is Identity (embeddings are pre-normed). Tokenizer is byte-level BPE (GPT-2 family), which the core NFKByteLevelBPETokenizer reads; the release ships only tokenizer.json, so vocab.json/merges.txt are extracted from it.

SmolVLM2-500M-Video-Instruct, 2.0 GB (Apache, ungated). SmolVLMForConditionalGeneration: a SigLIP vision encoder (hidden 768, patch 16, image 512) -> pixel-shuffle connector (scale_factor 4: 768*16=12288 -> Linear -> 960) -> a Llama decoder (VLlama3ForCausalLM, hidden 960, 32 layers, 15 heads, 5 kv, head_dim 64, tie true, model_type llama, which NFKMLXLanguageNet reads). image_token_id 49190 marks where the projected vision tokens splice into the text embeddings. Oracle: transformers' own SmolVLMForConditionalGeneration + AutoProcessor.

SmolLM2-135M-Instruct Q4_K_M GGUF, 105 MB (a small real quantized LLM). The test source for the native GGUF reader: a Q4_K_M model mixes Q4_K (most weights), Q6_K (embeddings/output), Q8_0, and F32 (norms), so one file exercises every dequantizer. IK_VAL_GGUF points at the file (config value is the relative path, joined to the directory).

Qwen3-VL-2B-Instruct, 4.25 GB. Qwen3VLForConditionalGeneration: a qwen3_vl ViT (depth 24, hidden 1024, 2D rotary, spatial_merge_size 2, deepstack layers 5/11/17) + a qwen3_vl_text decoder (Qwen3 blocks, hidden 2048/28 layers, but M-RoPE interleaved mrope_section [24,20,20] and deepstack injection at decoder layers 0/1/2). image_token_id 151655. Far more than SmolVLM: M-RoPE 3D positions and deepstack are real additions to the reused Qwen3 decoder.

The next dense Gemma 4 size: 42 layers, hidden 2560, 2 KV heads, kv-shared 18. 16 GB of bf16, which doubles past this machine's RAM at float32 - so its oracle runs under IK_GEMMA_DTYPE=bfloat16 and the Swift side loads at .checkpoint precision.

Structural only, like the Flash entry: shapes.json is built from the headers of the shards covering layers 0/3/60 plus the globals, fetched by HTTP range request (~1 MB against 400+ GB). The weights are never downloaded.

The LJSpeech-trained conformer FastSpeech2 and its 78-symbol ARPAbet vocabulary - the matching phoneme table the TTS chain needs. IK_VAL_FASTSPEECH2 is the .bin converted to safetensors (a passthrough that drops num_batches_tracked); the transformers implementation is the oracle.

MiniMax Music 3, the Diffusers-format release, fetched component by component as the port lands each stage (vocoder so far; condition_encoder, rvq_depth_decoder, transformer, language_model follow). The official checkpoint is already safetensors, so it is used in place: the Swift loader fuses the weight-norm pairs and transposes the conv layouts itself, and the diffusers implementation (>= 0.40.0, MiniMaxMusic3Vocoder et al.) is the oracle. THE WEIGHTS ARE NOT PERMISSIVELY LICENSED - the MiniMax-Music3 Community License requires UI attribution in commercial products and separate authorization above USD 20M yearly revenue; see Docs/companions.md and the LICENSE fetched beside the weights.
The multilingual byte-level BPE vocabulary, which the voice loop-closure test uses to read Whisper's transcription of the synthesized speech.

The LTX-Video DiT (2B), the denoising transformer. ~7.7 GB sharded. Loads directly (module keys mirror LTXVideoTransformer3DModel). Parity via run_reference.py ltx_transformer under the ltx oracle env, feeding recorded text embeddings (no T5).

T5-XXL v1.1 text encoder for LTX-Video (also the text encoder family for Wan/PixArt/SD3/Flux). ~19 GB fp32 sharded. Loads directly (keys mirror T5EncoderModel). Parity via run_reference.py ltx_t5 under the ltx oracle env.

RT-DETR r50vd object detector (Apache-2.0, the license-clean YOLO alternative). 172 MB single-file. Loads directly through NFKMLXRTDetr.loadWeights (model. prefix stripped, tied top-level heads and num_batches_tracked dropped, stage-1 stride-1 shortcut re-indexed). Real-weights parity via run_reference.py rtdetr_real under the llm oracle env; the tiny-config architecture parity is run_reference.py rtdetr (no weights).

RF-DETR base object detector (Roboflow, Apache-2.0): a windowed DINOv2-small backbone + C2f/RepVGG projector + two-stage Group-DETR deformable decoder, run at 560 (num_labels 91, decoder_n_points 2). At REFERENCE PARITY seam by seam on these released weights (testRFDetrMatchesTheReferenceOnReleasedWeights): every seam >=~1e-8 over the reference top-k, e2e within the top-k tie tolerance; the antialiased-bicubic pos-embed interp (a=-0.5, 37->40) was the one seam bug. The released file uses the ORIGINAL Roboflow naming (backbone.0.encoder.encoder.*, transformer.*, refpoint_embed, a fused self_attn.in_proj); NFKMLXRFDetr.loadWeights converts it on device (remapReferenceKey + the fused-qkv split), so it loads directly with no offline step. Registered in registerAll with the @objc download factories; the tests load this released file through loadWeights (IK_VAL_RFDETR). Real-weights parity via run_reference.py rf_detr_real --checkpoint <the directory> under the rfdetr oracle env (transformers 5.16.1); the tiny-config parity is run_reference.py rf_detr (no weights).

Parakeet-TDT 0.6B v2 speech recognizer (NVIDIA, CC-BY-4.0): a 2.47 GB .nemo tar holding model_config.yaml, model_weights.ckpt, and the SentencePiece BPE tokenizer (.model/.vocab). Unpack with `tar -xf` into raw/parakeet/tdt-0.6b-v2 (IK_VAL_PARAKEET); NFKMLXParakeet.backend(directoryURL:) reads model_weights.ckpt through the native torch reader and the *_tokenizer.vocab piece table. Parity via run_reference.py parakeet --checkpoint <the .nemo> under the nemo oracle env, on the validation speech clip (IK_VAL_AUDIO).

Chatterbox voice-cloning TTS (Resemble AI, MIT): VoiceEncoder (ve.safetensors, 7 MB), T3 (t3_cfg.safetensors, 2.1 GB, a Llama 520M), S3Gen with the S3 speech tokenizer under its tokenizer. subtree (s3gen.safetensors, 1.1 GB), the character-BPE tokenizer.json, and the built-in voice conds.pt. IK_VAL_CHATTERBOX is the directory itself; NFKMLXChatterboxTTS(directoryURL:) loads all five. Parity via run_reference.py chatterbox_voice / chatterbox_t3 / chatterbox_s3gen --checkpoint <the directory> under the chatterbox oracle env, on the validation speech clip (IK_VAL_AUDIO) as the voice prompt.

Kokoro-82M StyleTTS2/iSTFTNet TTS (Apache-2.0). 327 MB. The oracle vendors KModel + istftnet + modules from the pip `kokoro` package (torch/transformers/scipy, NO spaCy/misaki), running with phonemes supplied directly and the sine source's noise/phase zeroed for determinism. Loads directly through NFKMLXKokoro.loadWeights (module. prefix stripped, weight-norm fused, LSTMs folded, alpha ParameterLists stacked, ups transposed). Real-weights parity via run_reference.py kokoro under the llm oracle env. A voicepack .pt is a bare tensor: convert to a single-`voice` safetensors offline (Tools/kokoro-voice-to-safetensors) for NFKMLXKokoro.loadVoice.

MP-SENet speech enhancement (yxlu-0102/MP-SENet, MIT), 16 kHz g_best_dns. Not on HF: git-clone the repo to reference-sources/MP-SENet (its checkpoints and config.json ship with it), then convert best_ckpt/g_best_dns with Tools/mpsenet-to-safetensors (or the native .pth reader). The released core is a TS-TRANSFORMER (the repo's conformer.py is UNUSED): each block is norm1 -> nn.MultiheadAttention -> norm2 -> FFN(bidirectional nn.GRU + leaky_relu + linear) -> norm3. Parity via `run_reference.py mpsenet --checkpoint <g_best_dns>` with IK_MPSENET_SRC=<clone> and IK_MPSENET_CONFIG=<clone>/config.json, on the SOURCE (the MPSENet pip pkg needs Python >= 3.10; the source fallback runs on 3.9). THE bug was the batch_first trap: MHA and GRU are batch_first=False, so they run over axis 0 of the [B*F,T,C] reshape (fix = one transpose(1,0,2) in NFKMPSETransformer). At reference parity: waveform cosine > 0.999.

GTCRN ultra-light (~48.2K param) real-time speech enhancement (Xiaobin-Rong/gtcrn, MIT). Not on HF: git-clone the repo to reference-sources/gtcrn (checkpoints ship with it), then convert checkpoints/model_trained_on_dns3.tar with Tools/gtcrn-to-safetensors (or the native torch reader). STFT is n_fft=512/hop=256 with a SQRT-Hann window (hann_window(512).pow(0.5), from infer.py). Parity via `run_reference.py gtcrn --checkpoint <ckpt>` with IK_GTCRN_SRC=<clone>, on the source (torch only, runs on 3.9). Five load-bearing facts: erb_fc/ierb_fc are bias=False (fixed ERB filterbank); the deconv weight transpose is group-aware ([in,out/g,kH,kW] -> [out,kH,kW,in/g]); the shared NFKMLXGRUCell must add the n-gate hidden bias b_hn at step 0 (MLX's GRU omits it; PyTorch keeps it); the deconv front-pads time for BOTH conv and deconv with the ConvTranspose padding=(2*dilation,1) removing the excess (no crop); and MLX's GROUPED ConvTranspose does not match PyTorch, so a grouped deconv runs each group as its own groups=1 transpose. At reference parity: waveform cosine > 0.999, all seams (encoder/skips/dpgrnn/decoder) exact.

MossFormer2 SE 48K full-band speech enhancement (modelscope/ClearerVoice-Studio, Apache-2.0). Weights on HF (alibabasglab/MossFormer2_SE_48K/last_best_checkpoint.pt, keyed mossformer.*, loaded directly by the native .pth reader). The model SOURCE is not on HF: the mossformer2_se package files are fetched to reference-sources/clearervoice/models/mossformer2_se (curled, not cloned, to respect the repo git-clone safeguard). Oracle: `run_reference.py mossformer2_se --checkpoint <ckpt>` with IK_MOSSFORMER2_SE_SRC=<reference-sources/clearervoice>, on ~/.inferkit-validation/llmvenv (add rotary_embedding_torch + torchinfo). The fbank front end FORCES dither=0 (the released compute_fbank uses dither=1.0, random noise that makes parity impossible). Two load-bearing facts found on the M1: num_spks=2 (the wrapper builds MossFormer_MaskNet with the default, so conv1d_out widens to dModel*2 and the net returns speaker 0 -> the port slices the first dModel channels, exact because the 1x1 gated output/decoder are per-position); and the FLASH linear-attention path divides by the ORIGINAL sequence length n=x.shape[-2], NOT the padded length (only wrong when frames are not a multiple of group 256). At reference parity on the M1 (float32): fbank+delta 1.0, encoder and FLASH block0 0.99999994, FLASH block_last and the 961-bin mask 1.0, enhanced waveform 0.9999998. Parity test feeds the recorded feature to isolate the backbone from the Kaldi fbank.

DeepFilterNet3 real-time 48 kHz speech denoising (Rikorose/DeepFilterNet, dual MIT/Apache-2.0), the cheap counterpart to NFKMLXDenoiser (~2.3M params). NOT on HF and no offline converter: the `deepfilternet` pip package (deps `deepfilterlib` native Rust wheel + torch/torchaudio/numpy<2, Python 3.9) ships the weights and the libdf DSP. Build a dedicated venv `dfnvenv` (see oracle_environments.deepfilternet); `init_df()` downloads the DeepFilterNet3 model to ~/Library/Caches/DeepFilterNet/DeepFilterNet3 on first run. Oracle + weights in ONE command: `IK_DEEPFILTERNET_WEIGHTS_OUT=raw/deepfilternet/weights.safetensors dfnvenv/bin/python Tools/reference-parity/run_reference.py deepfilternet raw/deepfilternet/record.safetensors --checkpoint ~/Library/Caches/DeepFilterNet/DeepFilterNet3` — records the net boundary (spec/feat_erb/feat_spec in, e0..e3/emb/c0/m/df_coefs/spec_e/lsnr, the ERB banks) plus the enhance() waveform, AND dumps model.state_dict() (dropping num_batches_tracked) as the weights. The NET (DfNet) is a clean torch nn.Module validated seam by seam; the STFT/ERB/normalization DSP is Rust libdf, reproduced in NFKMLXDeepFilterNetDSP (Vorbis window sin(pi/2 sin^2(pi(n+0.5)/N)), analysis scale 1/N left-pad nFFT-hop; ERB feature 10log10(|spec|^2 erb_fb+1e-10) then EMA mean-norm (x-s)/40 init linspace(-60,-90,32); unit_norm x/sqrt(s) init linspace(0.001,0.0001,96); synthesis irfft(spec*N) window-squared OLA). ONE ORACLE TRAP: df_state.synthesis(as_complex(spec_e).numpy()) writes IN PLACE through the view, so snapshot spec_e BEFORE synthesis. At reference parity on the released DeepFilterNet3 weights: every net seam exact (1.0000000), DSP features exact (1.0000000), enhanced waveform 0.9999999.

VoiceRestore (skirdey/voicerestore, MIT), a ~301M flow-matching universal speech restorer (noise+reverb+clip+bandlimit), E2-TTS-derived. Weights: jadechoghari/VoiceRestore/pytorch_model.bin (the transformer, keyed transformer.*/proj_in/cond_proj/to_pred, loaded by the native torch reader; abs_pos_emb is 2000 rows -- convert to weights.safetensors with the vrvenv once) + nvidia/bigvgan_v2_24khz_100band_256x/bigvgan_generator.pt (the vocoder). SOURCE (git-clone-safeguard: curl, don't clone) to reference-sources/voicerestore: voice_restore.py + tensor_typing.py from the HF repo, and the bundled BigVGAN/ package (bigvgan.py, activations.py, meldataset.py, env.py, utils.py, alias_free_activation/torch/*, configs/bigvgan_v2_24khz_100band_256x.json, plus an empty __init__.py). Oracle env vrvenv (Python 3.9, torch 2.2.2, x-transformers==1.34.0 + gateloop-transformer==0.2.5 + rotary-embedding-torch==0.8.3 + torchdiffeq==0.2.4 + jaxtyping + BigVGAN deps matplotlib/tqdm/huggingface_hub -- see oracle_environments.voicerestore). THREE modes: `run_reference.py voicerestore --checkpoint pytorch_model.bin` with IK_VR_SRC=<reference-sources/voicerestore> records the transformer seams (x_in, per-block gateloop/attn/ff, velocity, null velocity); `run_reference.py bigvgan --checkpoint bigvgan_generator.pt` records mel->waveform; `IK_VR_BIGVGAN=<generator> run_reference.py voicerestore_e2e --checkpoint pytorch_model.bin` records the BigVGAN-mel + midpoint-CFM-sampler(seeded y0) + vocoder end to end. THE ORACLE BUG (the transformer was correct as written): the seam hooks fire during BOTH the conditioned velocity pass and the CFG null pass -- remove the hooks BEFORE the null pass or the null seams overwrite the conditioned ones. SimpleGateLoopLayer = RMSNorm + Linear(dim,3dim) -> q/kv/a, sigmoid gate a, recurrence h_t=a_t*h_{t-1}+kv_t (sequential = exact), out q_t*h_t, run residual. At reference parity: transformer every seam 0.99999994-1.0, BigVGAN waveform 0.9999997, e2e mel 1.0 / restored 0.9999999 / waveform ~1.0.

Resemble Enhance (resemble-ai, MIT), a five-network general speech restorer (fixes noise + reverberation + clipping + band-limiting together). Weights on HF (ResembleAI/resemble-enhance/enhancer_stage2, the DeepSpeed shard ds/G/default/mp_rank_00_model_states.pt keyed `module`, ~713 MB; nest under module. so the loader strips that prefix). It uses OLD weight_g/weight_v weight-norm, which fusedWeightNorm handles; the source builds modules with the parametrization API, so the ORACLE renames weight_g/v -> parametrizations.weight.original0/1 before a strict load. SOURCE (git-clone-safeguard: cp the cloned tree) to reference-sources/resemble-enhance/resemble_enhance; the oracle imports leaf modules (melspec/common/enhancer.lcfm/enhancer.univnet/denoiser) directly to AVOID deepspeed (which the top-level enhancer.py pulls via utils.distributed). Oracle env reenhancevenv (Python 3.12, torch/torchaudio/scipy/omegaconf/matplotlib/pandas/rich/librosa, numpy<2; see oracle_environments.reenhance). SIX modes, all --checkpoint the mp_rank shard with IK_REENHANCE_SRC=<reference-sources/resemble-enhance>: reenhance_mel (torchaudio magnitude mel + preemphasis + amp-to-db + headroom normalize), reenhance_irmae (encode/decode), reenhance_cfm (WaveNet velocity seam + the exponential-decay midpoint sampler nfe=32), reenhance_univnet (LVC vocoder with a recorded noise z), reenhance_denoiser (STFT-mask 2D UNet wav->wav), reenhance_e2e (the full enhance() path lambd=0.5/tau=0.5/nfe=32 with recorded tau/vocoder noises). Records write to ~/.inferkit-validation/records/reenhance_*.safetensors; IK_PARITY_REENHANCE is that DIRECTORY. THE load-bearing facts, all found by seam localization: the KernelPredictor's LeakyReLU is slope 0.2 (LVCBlock overrides the KernelPredictor's own 0.1 default) -- with 0.1 the vocoder scores ~0.84; the LVCBlock convt_pre is Sequential(LeakyReLU, ConvTranspose) so the activation runs BEFORE the transposed conv; and _reenhance_hp MUST load the released hparams.yaml because the enhancer default lcfm_z_scale is 5 but the release is 6, which is cosine-invisible (it changes only the prior/noise blend magnitude) and only surfaces in the e2e. The LVC (location-variable convolution, dilation 1) is a per-segment im2col matmul (MLX has no unfold). At reference parity on the released weights: mel 0.9999998, IRMAE encode 0.9999985 / decode 1.0000002, CFM velocity 1.0000001 / sample 1.0000001, UnivNet 0.9999365, denoiser 0.9999996, end-to-end waveform 0.9999971.

SGMSE+ score-based generative speech enhancement / dereverberation (sp-uhh/sgmse, MIT), the generative anchor of the restoration vein. AT REFERENCE PARITY on the released EMA weights: the score net (NFKMLXNCSNppNet) net-seam cosine = 1.000000000000 (and the input-conv seam) on BOTH released backbone variants. git-clone the repo to reference-sources/sgmse (= IK_SGMSE_SRC, the oracle+converter source). CHECKPOINTS ARE ON HUGGING FACE (no GDrive needed): the CLASSIC 'ncsnpp' VoiceBank checkpoint is sp-uhh/speech-enhancement-sgmse/train_vb_29nqe0uh_epoch=115.ckpt (theta 1.5, sigma_min 0.05, sigma_max 0.5, n_fft 510/hop 128, attn@16, progressive output_skip/input_skip, window='hann' -> windowPower 1.0) — this is the CANONICAL validation asset (weights.safetensors/record.safetensors); the WSJ0-REVERB dereverb checkpoint is Spatium3d/sgmse_wsj0/train_wsj0_2cta4cov_epoch=159.ckpt. A SECOND released variant, 'ncsnpp_48k' (progressive='none', NO attention, plain Hann, n_fft 1534, and the output projection applied BEFORE the sigma division), is the ReverbFX sgmse_artificial_rir_350k.ckpt (www2.informatik.uni-hamburg.de/sp/audio/publications/itg2025-reverbfx/checkpoints/) — also at parity. The port is config-driven for both (progressiveOutputSkip + windowPower + attentionResolutions), and the oracle records the geometry so the Swift test builds a matching config from the record. INFERENCE READS THE EMA WEIGHTS: Tools/sgmse-to-safetensors lets torch_ema apply them (model.eval() -> ema.copy_to(dnn)) then dumps dnn.state_dict() (all_modules.N.* / output_layer.*). This port implements backbone='ncsnpp' and 'ncsnpp_48k'; 'ncsnpp_v2' (a different two-arg forward) is out of scope. Convert: IK_SGMSE_SRC=<clone> python Tools/sgmse-to-safetensors/convert.py <ckpt> weights.safetensors. Parity: IK_SGMSE_SRC=<clone> python Tools/reference-parity/run_reference.py sgmse record.safetensors --checkpoint <ckpt>, then set IK_VAL_SGMSE/IK_PARITY_SGMSE and run NFKMLXSGMSETests. TRAP: torch>=2.6 defaults weights_only=True and refuses the pickled data module — the converter+oracle patch torch.load to weights_only=False. A sampled clip is not bitwise-comparable (random stream); the net seam is the ground and e2e asserts signal.

StoRM stochastic-regeneration speech enhancement / dereverberation (sp-uhh/storm, MIT), a FEW-STEP follow-on on SGMSE+ (NFKMLXStoRM). AT REFERENCE PARITY at a tiny random configuration: the discriminative-predictor seam and the conditioned-score seam both cosine 1.000000000000. git-clone the repo to reference-sources/storm (= IK_STORM_SRC). Parity is TINY-RANDOM (no download needed, the LTX/Wan/Z-Image method): `run_reference.py storm record.safetensors` with IK_STORM_SRC=<clone> builds StoRM's two NCSN++ networks from the backbone registry (a discriminative predictor input_channels=2, a condition='both' score net input_channels=6), randomizes them, and SAVES both nets' weights into the record under w::denoiser_net.* / w::score_net.*, plus the geometry (cfg_*) and the denoiser/score seams; the Swift test (NFKMLXStoRMTests, gated on IK_PARITY_STORM alone) loads the w:: weights and compares. This validates the NEW two-net architecture; the NCSN++ backbone is already at released-weight parity via SGMSE+ (net_out 1.0). ORACLE TRAP: the storm clone omits upfirdn2d_native.py and its op imports the FUSED CUDA extension (needs ninja), so the oracle injects an inline native upfirdn2d + a leaky-ReLU shim into sys.modules before importing the backbone; also needs h5py (storm data_module) and the torch>=2.6 weights_only patch. RELEASED combined StochasticRegenerationModel checkpoints are GDrive-only (folder 1ExFm97obaXTYFoBApWjbK_ypxTP-Cgdq: TIMIT+Chime3, WSJ0+Chime3, VB-DEMAND, WSJ0+Reverb dereverb, WSJ0+Wind); the NCSN++M/<task> folders there are SCORE-ONLY (single dnn.) not combined. Converter Tools/storm-to-safetensors dumps denoiser_net.*/score_net.* EMA for a combined ckpt when one is obtained. This port implements backbone='ncsnpp'; 'ncsnpp_v2' is out of scope.

BiRefNet (ZhengPeng7, MIT): high-resolution dichotomous segmentation for background removal, at REFERENCE PARITY end to end on this released model.safetensors (fp16), validated seam by seam in NFKMLXReferenceParityTests: the deformable conv vs torchvision (testDeformableConv2dMatchesTorchvision, run_reference.py dcn — no weights, system torchvision), the Swin-v1-L backbone (testSwinBackboneMatchesTheReference, run_reference.py birefnet_backbone), the neck = mul_scl_ipt + cxt + the ASPPDeformable squeeze (testBiRefNetNeckMatchesTheReference, run_reference.py birefnet_neck), the decoder (testBiRefNetDecoderMatchesTheReference, run_reference.py birefnet_decode), and the assembled model (testBiRefNetEndToEndMatchesTheReference, reuses the decode record). Every seam ~1e-12. NFKMLXBiRefNet loads this file directly (loadWeights routes bb./squeeze_module.->encoder, decoder.->decoder, drops relative_position_index / num_batches_tracked / the training-only gdt_pred and conv_ms_spvn heads, and upcasts fp16->float32); it MUST train(false) after loading or the squeeze/decoder BatchNorms use batch stats (the backbone is all LayerNorm, which masks the bug). The reference is the vendored BiRefNet code, COMMITTED at Tools/reference-parity/refsrc: refsrc/birefnet/swin_v1.py (+ a config stub, SDPA disabled) for the backbone oracle, and refsrc/birefnet_hf/ (the HF single-file birefnet.py + BiRefNet_config.py, with the training-only kornia laplacian import stubbed) for the full-model oracles. run_reference.py defaults IK_REF_SRC to that committed dir, so the birefnet_* modes run with IK_REF_SRC unset. Needs system torch + timm + torchvision + einops + transformers (PretrainedConfig). Registered in registerAll; the @objc factories load IK_VAL_BIREFNET. The IK_PARITY_BIREFNET_{BACKBONE,NECK,DECODE} records are generated by the modes above (parity/*.safetensors) and their paths set in the local config JSON.

gpt-oss-20b, 13.8 GB (Apache-2.0). GptOssForCausalLM: 24 layers alternating sliding-window (128) and full attention, a learned attention sink per head, biases on every attention projection, a 32-expert top-4 mixture whose router carries a bias and takes the softmax over the selected logits, fused interleaved gate_up experts with biases and the clamped SwiGLU (limit 7, alpha 1.702), YaRN rotary with truncate false. The experts ship MXFP4 (`*_blocks` uint8 [E, out, in/32, 16] + `*_scales` e8m0 uint8), which the loader feeds to MLX's mxfp4 mode packed; attention, embeddings, and the head are bf16. Tokenizer: o200k_harmony byte-level BPE in tokenizer.json only. Oracle: transformers' GptOssForCausalLM at a tiny config (the 20B does not fit an oracle here); the MXFP4 decode is measured on real bytes.

MetricGAN+ (speechbrain, Apache-2.0), 7.6 MB: a two-layer bidirectional LSTM (200) over log1p-magnitude frames of a 512-point zero-padded Hamming STFT at hop 256, Linear 400→300, LeakyReLU 0.3, Linear 300→257, a per-bin learnable sigmoid 1.2·sigmoid(slope·x); the mask times the features, expm1, the noisy phase, iSTFT, peak-normalized. The release is a plain state dict the native torch reader opens; the LSTMs fold into MLX Wx/Wh/bias. example.wav is the model card's own noisy clip, the parity input. Oracle: speechbrain's SpectralMaskEnhancement (llm env + the speechbrain package).

CMGAN (ruizhecao96/CMGAN, MIT), 7.5 MB: the released TSCNet generator (dense encoder, four two-stage conformer blocks with Shaw's relative position embedding, mask + complex decoders) over a mag^0.3 compressed 400/100 Hamming STFT. A plain state dict the native torch reader opens. p232_052_noisy.wav is one of the repository's own noisy VCTK-DEMAND samples, the parity input. Oracle: the repository's src/ (models/, utils.py) on the llm env with einops; IK_CMGAN_SRC names it.

FRCRN SE 16K (ClearerVoice, Apache-2.0), 161 MB: two complex UNets over a 640/320 sqrt-Hann conv-STFT with frequency-recurrent FSMN memories, complex squeeze-excites, and a time FSMN bottleneck. The `model` dict of the checkpoint (a plain state dict the native torch reader opens); every stage is stored twice (flat attributes and ModuleLists) and the loader keeps the lists. Oracle: ClearerVoice's models/frcrn_se/ sources (curled into reference-sources/clearervoice, IK_FRCRN_SRC) on the llm env; the parity input is the CMGAN noisy clip.

MossFormer2 SR 48K (ClearerVoice, Apache-2.0), 2 × 220 MB: the mel-to-mel MossFormer2 backbone (a {'mossformer': state} container, a doubled prefix the loader strips) and the weight-normed Snake HiFi-GAN generator ({'generator': state}). Oracle: ClearerVoice's models/mossformer2_sr/, dataloader/meldataset.py (needs pydub), utils/bandwidth_sub.py, and config/inference/MossFormer2_SR_48K.json curled into reference-sources/clearervoice (IK_MOSSFORMER2_SR_SRC), on the llm env; the parity input is the CMGAN clean clip resampled to 48 kHz.

NU-Wave 2 (maum-ai/nuwave2, BSD-3), 20.9 MB: the README's official Lightning checkpoint (state_dict under model.model.; the pickled callbacks are inert to the native torch reader, and need a pytorch_lightning stub under torch.load). Oracle: the repository's model.py / diffusion.py / hparameter.yaml curled into reference-sources/nuwave2 (IK_NUWAVE2_SRC) on the llm env with omegaconf; torch.istft is patched to take the complex view. The parity input is the CMGAN clean 16 kHz clip through inference.py's conditioning.

Apollo (JusperLee/Apollo, CC-BY-SA-4.0 code and weights), 66 MB: the released look2hear Apollo (80-band split of an 882/441 STFT, six band-Roformer + ICB layers, GLU band heads), a state_dict container the native torch reader unwraps. input_wav.wav is the repository's own 44.1 kHz stereo sample; the parity reads channel 0 for two seconds. Oracle: the repository's look2hear package curled into reference-sources/apollo (IK_APOLLO_SRC) on the llm env (needs huggingface_hub, soundfile).

Gemma 3 270M instruct (gemma3_text, 536 MB bf16). google/gemma-3-* is gated; unsloth/gemma-3-*-it are faithful ungated mirrors. The decoder NFKMLXGemma3Net runs: (1+w) RMS norms, sandwich blocks, 5:1 sliding/full pattern (window 512, local rope 10000 / global 1e6, no scaling), per-head QK norm, GeGLU gelu_tanh, tied head, no softcaps. The record (run_reference.py gemma3 <out> --checkpoint <this>, gemma oracle env) carries the prompt ids, every hidden state, the logits, the greedy continuation the reference decodes through its hybrid cache, the chat-templated ids, and six tokenizer probes.
Gemma 3 1B instruct (gemma3_text, 2.0 GB bf16): 26 layers, hidden 1152, 4 heads over 1 KV head, intermediate 6912, the same window and rope as the 270M. Same record layout as GEMMA3_270M.

Gemma 3 4B instruct (gemma3, multimodal, 8.6 GB bf16 sharded; ~17 GB at float32). Gemma3ForConditionalGeneration: a SigLIP so400m vision tower (hidden 1152, 27 layers, 16 heads, patch 14 at 896 -> 4096 patches) under vision_tower.vision_model., a multi_modal_projector (4x4 average pool to 256 soft tokens, a (1+w) RMS norm, one [1152, 2560] matrix), and the decoder under language_model.model. (34 layers, hidden 2560, 8 heads over 4 KV heads, window 1024, the global layers' rope stretched by linear factor 8, vocab 262208). The released file is in the transformers 4.x key layout; a 5.x-written one nests the same under model.*, and the loader reads both. Three records: gemma3 (text-only logits + continuation), gemma3_vision_real (the plate through the release's own image processor, then the tower and projector loaded selectively: patch embeddings, layer 0, the tower output, the 256 soft tokens), and gemma3_conditional_real (the processor's chat prompt with the image expanded to 

<start_of_image> + 256 soft tokens + <end_of_image>

, the argmax at every fused position, the last-16 logits, every hidden state, the greedy continuation). Both image records use --image inputs/subject384.jpg --size 384.

Gemma 3n E2B instruct (gemma3n, tri-modal, 10 GB bf16 sharded across three files; ~21 GB at float32, so the oracle and the test run as separate processes). 1556 tensors: 731 the decoder under model.language_model. (30 layers, hidden 2048, 8 heads over 2 KV heads at head_dim 256, four sliding layers to one full, num_kv_shared_layers 10, altup_num_inputs 4, laurel_rank 64, hidden_size_per_layer_input 256 over a 262144-row table, activation_sparsity_pattern 0.95 on the first ten layers, vocab 262400 with final_logit_softcapping 30), 548 the MobileNetV5-300M vision tower under model.vision_tower.timm_model. (reached through timm, not transformers, so the gemma oracle carries `timm`), 269 the Universal Speech Model Conformer under model.audio_tower. (hidden 1536, 12 blocks, chunk 12, left context 13, right 0, reduction 4), and 8 the two multimodal embedders. Seven records: gemma3n_tiny (a random tiny configuration carrying every mechanism — AltUp, LAuReL, per-layer embeddings, activation sparsity on two of six layers, and a shared-key-value tail holding one sliding and one full layer — with every hidden state and the cached greedy continuation), gemma3n (the released decoder's logits, every hidden state, and the continuation), gemma3n_audio (a tiny encoder with a NON-ZERO right context, which the release never exercises, plus a padded tail), gemma3n_audio_real (the released tower on a deterministic random mel, with the first block's four seams recorded so a divergence lands on a branch), gemma3n_vision_real (the released tower on a deterministic random frame in 0...1, every stage plus the fused grid, and the multimodal embedder's weights), gemma3n_mel (the release's own feature extractor), and gemma3n_conditional_real (the whole model: the processor's 272-id prompt and its pixel values, the argmax at every fused position, the last-16 logits, and the greedy continuation). The image and audio records use deterministic random inputs rather than a plate, which keeps the resize — PIL there, CoreGraphics here — out of the comparison. The gated google/gemma-3n-* are mirrored ungated here. E4B is the same architecture at 35 layers.

Depth Anything 3 BASE (vitb: 768/12/12, DualDPT 128 over [96,192,384,768]; `.base`). All 437 tensors load, every branch (depth, aux/ray, cam_dec, cam_enc). RT-DETRv2 r50vd (`.v2R50VD`), the v2 retrain of the r50vd geometry. RT-DETRv2 (RTDetrV2ForObjectDetection, Apache-2.0) runs through NFKMLXRTDetr: v2 changes only the deformable decoder's sampling, carried by NFKMLXRTDetrConfiguration.decoderOffsetScale and .decoderMethod (NFKMLXRTDetrSamplingMethod bilinear/discrete). Every released v2 config repeats its RT-DETR namesake's geometry and states the RT-DETR sampling settings (decoder_method default, decoder_offset_scale 0.5), so the four v2 presets return their v1 counterparts and the releases differ only in their weights. Record: `run_reference.py rtdetr_v2_real --checkpoint <this directory> --image subject384.jpg --size 640` (llm env) -> IK_PARITY_RTDETR_V2_R50VD; one real mode serves all four sizes. The tiny-config parity is `run_reference.py rtdetr_v2` (no weights) -> IK_PARITY_RTDETR_V2, which sets decoder_method discrete and an offset scale of 0.35 so the discrete sampling path and a non-default offset scale are exercised.

Gemma 3n E4B (16 GB bf16): 35 layers, fifteen sharing keys and values, at the E2B's widths and towers; read by the E2B's configuration reader. Measured at bf16 on both sides (`IK_GEMMA_DTYPE=bfloat16 run_reference.py gemma3n --checkpoint <this directory>`, gemma env), the Gemma 4 E4B treatment: logit cosine 0.99989, argmax 5/6, the one flip at a half-logit reference margin. The E2B recorded the same way (IK_PARITY_GEMMA3N_E2B_BF16, the same command on the E2B directory) is the control: exact at float32, it reads 0.99989 at bf16 too, so that is the rounding floor the E4B is held to.

ViTPose base with the SIMPLE decoder (ViTAE-Transformer, Apache-2.0), a plain ViT-B backbone under a ReLU + bilinear upsample + 3x3 convolution head, at 256x192 with patch 16. Loads directly through NFKMLXVitPose.loadWeights (the module keys are the checkpoint's; only the convolution layouts move). Two load-bearing facts: the patch-embedding convolution pads by 2, which at this geometry leaves the patch count at 16x12 either way, so a plain non-overlapping patchify loads cleanly and samples every window two pixels early (a wrong patchify scores the backbone 0.998 instead of 0.9999999999); and the position table carries a class-token row the sequence does not, added to every patch as a constant bias (pos[:, 1:] + pos[:, :1]). The backbone layer_norm_eps is 1e-12, not a ViT's usual 1e-6. Record: `run_reference.py vitpose --checkpoint <this directory>` (llm env, needs Pillow) -> IK_PARITY_VITPOSE; one mode serves both released decoders, since the geometry comes from each release's config.json. The oracle resizes and normalizes the image itself rather than through VitPoseImageProcessor, which warps a person's BOX through an affine transform that a whole-image caller has no box for, and records the prepared pixels, the backbone feature map, the heatmaps, the integer peaks, the DARK-refined keypoints, and the scores. The DARK decode (post_dark_unbiased_data_processing) is ported in full: keypoints_from_heatmaps defaults kernel=11 (Gaussian radius 5) while the callee's own signature defaults to 3, and scipy's default reflect mode is SYMMETRIC where mirror is not, so the blur's border gathers reflected indices. At reference parity on these released weights (testVitPoseMatchesTheReference): backbone feature map 0.9999999999995017, heatmaps 0.9999999999966225, every integer peak exact, the refinement within 8.80751758813858e-05 of a cell. vitpose-plus-* releases route the feed-forward through per-dataset experts and need a dataset index at inference; the configuration reader refuses them.

ViTPose base with the CLASSIC decoder (`.base`): the same ViT-B backbone under two transposed-convolution blocks (no bias, each followed by a BatchNorm and a ReLU) and a 1x1 convolution, which is the head SimpleBaseline uses; use_simple_decoder in the release's config.json selects it. Record: `run_reference.py vitpose --checkpoint <this directory>` (llm env) -> IK_PARITY_VITPOSE_BASE. At reference parity on these released weights: feature map 0.9999999999931072, heatmaps 0.9999999999953517, every integer peak exact, refinement within 4.622340202331543e-05 of a cell. This release is what showed that the DARK refinement must NOT be clamped: a flat neighborhood can move a peak past its own heatmap, and clamping the shift to one cell disagreed with the reference by 1.04 cells, so NFKMLXVitPoseNet.estimate clamps the final normalized position instead, because NFKKeypoint promises one.

DDColor (piddnad/DDColor, Apache-2.0), the modern colorizer beside the 2016 and 2017 ports: a ConvNeXt-L encoder (depths [3,3,27,3], widths [192,384,768,1536]) hooked at its four stages, a spectral-normalized U-Net decoder (three UnetBlockWide blocks over CustomPixelShuffle_ICNR, then a last pixel shuffle at scale 4 for the pixel embedding), and a Mask2Former-style color decoder (100 learned color queries cross-attending the three U-Net stage outputs over nine layers, dotted against the pixel embedding into one color attention map each, read by a final 1x1 convolution beside the input). The three released .pth checkpoints are the NFKMLXDDColorVariant cases (.modelscope, .paper, .artistic), loaded by the native torch reader. Coverage on ddcolor_modelscope.pth: 573 built parameters all loaded, 31 released tensors deliberately dropped (the weight_u/weight_v power-iteration vectors the spectral-norm fusion consumes, the encoder's classification head and its pooled norm, the normalization buffers the port applies itself, and the BatchNorm step counters), 0 unaccounted. Oracle: `run_reference.py ddcolor --checkpoint <release .pth>` on the llm env (which gained scikit-image). The reference is not in transformers, so IK_DDCOLOR_SRC names the cloned repository's basicsr/ directory (ddcolor_arch.py plus ddcolor_arch_utils/) and the oracle stubs basicsr's registry so the import stays to the architecture itself; the record carries the prepared gray pixels, the lightness, the four hooked encoder features, the three U-Net stage outputs, the pixel embedding, the color attention maps, and the chroma. THE load-bearing facts: forward_features calls each norm{i} for its hook's side effect only (the assignment back to x is commented out), so the trunk carries the un-normalized stage output forward; spectral_norm stores weight_orig beside weight_u/weight_v and in eval mode divides by u^T W v using the vectors as stored, which the loader fuses; custom_conv_layer builds an nn.Sequential where a ReLU slot still consumes its index (a BatchNorm after an activation lands at 2, one with no activation before it at 1); and those Sequentials are held as [Module] arrays, because MLX parses a numeric @ModuleInfo key as an array index and aborts the process when the checkpoint's list meets a child module. At reference parity on ddcolor_modelscope.pth: hooks 0.9999999999961443 / 0.9999999999975543 / 0.999999999986007 / 0.9999999999450404, U-Net stages 0.9999999998703757 / 0.9999999998944228 / 0.9999999999032585, pixel embedding 0.9999999999013038, color attention maps 0.9999999998470392, chroma 0.9999999998455213.

SmolVLM2-256M-Video-Instruct (Apache, ungated), the smallest released size. NFKMLXSmolVLM.release(directoryURL:) reads the SigLIP geometry, the pixel-shuffle factor, the tile size and the tokens per tile from this config.json, so no preset is hard-coded. Record: `run_reference.py smolvlm` with the directory -> IK_PARITY_SMOLVLM_256M.

SmolVLM2-2.2B-Instruct (Apache, ungated), the largest released size, sharded across two files that NFKMLXReleaseWeights reads. Its text config states no `num_attention_heads`, so the language reader derives the head count from `head_dim` (32) rather than falling back to 16; the wrong count would have loaded silently. Record: `run_reference.py smolvlm` with the directory -> IK_PARITY_SMOLVLM_2_2B.

oracle_environments.comment: diffusers cannot be installed beside the other oracles — it needs a newer transformers than the 4.33.3 the Whisper / CLIP / SegFormer records were measured against — so the `sd_*` modes of Tools/reference-parity/run_reference.py run under their own interpreter.

diffusers.create: python3 -m venv sdvenv && ./sdvenv/bin/pip install "diffusers==0.31.0" "transformers==4.46.3" "torch==2.8.0" safetensors accelerate

llm.why: Qwen3 needs transformers >= 4.51; the vision oracles run against 4.33.3 and the diffusers oracle against its own environment, so a third one keeps them from fighting. The SmolVLM oracle additionally needs Pillow, torchvision, and num2words for its image processor, and the DDColor oracle needs scikit-image for its Lab conversion, and the HAT oracle needs einops (basicsr itself is shimmed in the mode rather than installed).
llm.rebuild: python3 -m venv ~/.inferkit-validation/llmvenv && ~/.inferkit-validation/llmvenv/bin/python3 -m pip install 'transformers>=4.51' torch safetensors Pillow torchvision num2words gguf accelerate 'silero-vad' 'torchaudio==2.8.0' 'descript-audio-codec' 'snac' scikit-image einops

voicerestore.why: VoiceRestore's reference pins x-transformers==1.34.0 + gateloop-transformer==0.2.5 + rotary-embedding-torch==0.8.3 + torchdiffeq==0.2.4 (newer x-transformers changed signatures and swapped the gateloop layer), which would fight the other oracles, so it runs under its own interpreter on Python 3.9. The bundled BigVGAN package additionally needs matplotlib/tqdm/huggingface_hub, and the transformer source needs jaxtyping.
voicerestore.rebuild: python3 -m venv ~/.inferkit-validation/vrvenv && ~/.inferkit-validation/vrvenv/bin/pip install 'numpy<2' 'torch==2.2.2' 'torchaudio==2.2.2' 'x-transformers==1.34.0' 'gateloop-transformer==0.2.5' 'rotary-embedding-torch==0.8.3' 'torchdiffeq==0.2.4' einops safetensors librosa scipy soundfile jaxtyping beartype matplotlib tqdm huggingface_hub

reenhance.why: Resemble Enhance is not on PyPI as an importable inference package without deepspeed (its top-level enhancer.py pulls deepspeed via utils.distributed, which is painful on macOS), so the oracle vendors the resemble_enhance package source and imports only the leaf modules (melspec/common/enhancer.lcfm/enhancer.univnet/denoiser), which avoid deepspeed. Its own interpreter keeps torchaudio 2.11 / numpy<2 from fighting the other oracles. Needs tqdm (cfm.py imports it) and the omegaconf/rich/pandas/matplotlib the source imports at module load.
reenhance.rebuild: /opt/homebrew/opt/python@3.12/bin/python3.12 -m venv ~/.inferkit-validation/reenhancevenv && ~/.inferkit-validation/reenhancevenv/bin/pip install 'numpy<2' torch torchaudio scipy omegaconf matplotlib pandas rich librosa safetensors tqdm

Set IK_REF_SRC to the unpacked `depth_anything_3` package directory (the pip wheel: `pip download depth_anything_3` then unzip).

The ControlNet oracles record BOTH the ControlNet (w::) and the base transformer (t::) at tiny random configs and the base-with-residuals output, so the Swift side validates the per-block residuals AND the base injection (SD3 interval_control non-ceil, FLUX ceil). flux_controlnet_hint additionally exercises the input_hint_block (the ControlNetConditioningEmbedding pyramid over a full-resolution control image, 8x downsample to the packed grid). IK_PARITY_SD3_CONTROLNET / _SINGLE / IK_PARITY_FLUX_CONTROLNET / _HINT are records/*.safetensors, tiny-random (no download).

chatterbox.why: chatterbox-tts pins torch 2.6 / torchaudio 2.6 / transformers 5.x and pulls s3tokenizer, librosa, and perth, which would fight the other oracles' pins, so it runs under its own interpreter on Homebrew's python@3.12. transformers 5.x also serves the rope_scaling mode (the oracle Config carries both rope_scaling and rope_parameters).

rfdetr.why: RF-DETR (RfDetrForObjectDetection) landed in transformers 5.16, newer than the llm oracle's pin (which serves rtdetr/rtdetr_real), so it runs under its own interpreter. The tiny rf_detr mode needs no weights; rf_detr_real loads the released Roboflow/rf-detr-base checkpoint and its image processor (Pillow).

ultralytics.why: The YOLO oracles read ultralytics' own model, and the released .pt files carry a pickled module rather than a bare state dict, so the package that wrote them has to import them. It sits on the system interpreter here, outside the virtual environments the other oracles use. Version 8.4.120 supports every generation this port covers, including YOLO26.

shapes_comment: Releases held to the module STRUCTURALLY (every parameter's shape against the safetensors headers, no weights downloaded): `python3 shapes.py <repo> ~/.inferkit-validation/shapes/<directory>`; `IK_SHAPES_ROOT` names the parent, and NFKMLXReleasedSizesTests reads each entry by directory name.

shapes.note: SD3.5-large (8B) transformer. The official stabilityai repo is gated; this is an ungated mirror of the same geometry. Python's urllib hangs on HF's redirect here, so capture the headers with curl range requests rather than shapes.py.
SD3.5-medium (2.5B, MMDiT-X) transformer, which exercises the dual-attention path (attn2 on the first thirteen layers). Ungated mirror.
FLUX.1 [schnell] (12B) transformer. Ungated mirror of the Apache release.
FLUX.1 [dev] (12B) transformer, guidance-distilled (the guidance_embedder the schnell size lacks). The official BFL repo is gated; this is an ungated mirror.
